question: In which of the following valleys, over 97% of India's coal reserves are located?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Damodar, Sone, Mahanadi and Godavari Valleys**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India’s coal reserves:** Over **97% of India's coal reserves** are concentrated in the valleys of **Damodar, Sone, Mahanadi, and Godavari**, making them the most significant coal-bearing regions.
 
• **Damodar Valley:** Known as the **"Ruhr of India"**, it is one of the primary coal-producing regions, spanning states like **Jharkhand** and **West Bengal**. Major coalfields include **Jharia, Bokaro, and Raniganj**.
 
• **Sone Valley:** Located in **Madhya Pradesh**, this valley hosts significant coal reserves, contributing to India’s energy sector.
 
• **Mahanadi Valley:** Found in **Odisha**, major coalfields like **Talcher** and **Ib Valley** are situated here. This region is a key supplier of thermal coal for power generation.
 
• **Godavari Valley:** Located in **Telangana** and **Andhra Pradesh**, the **Singareni coalfields** are prominent here, known for producing high-grade coal.
 
• **Economic significance:** These valleys play a crucial role in India’s energy security, as coal is the primary source for electricity generation and industrial processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Damodar Valley:**

 
 
• It is known for its historical coal mining activities dating back to colonial times.
 
• Major coalfields include **Jharia** (famous for its coking coal), **Bokaro**, and **Raniganj**.
 
• Coal from this region is extensively used in steel production and thermal power generation.
 
 
 
• **Sone Valley:**
 
 
• This valley is located primarily in **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It contains coalfields like **Singrauli**, which supply coal for power plants such as NTPC Singrauli.
 
 
 
• **Mahanadi Valley:**
 
 
• Located in **Odisha**, it includes major coalfields such as **Talcher** and **Ib Valley**.
 
• Coal from this region is used for thermal power generation and industrial purposes.
 
 
 
• **Godavari Valley:**
 
 
• This valley spans **Telangana** and **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It is home to the **Singareni Collieries**, which produce high-quality coal.
 
• Coal from this region is used in power plants and other industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Coal:**
 
 
• Coal contributes to over **55%** of India’s electricity generation.
 
• India ranks as the **second-largest coal producer** globally, after China.
 
• Coal is vital for industries like steel, cement, and chemicals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Coal Types in India:**

 
 
• **Anthracite:** Found in small quantities; used for heating purposes.
 
• **Bituminous:** Most abundant type; used in power generation and industries.
 
• **Lignite:** Found in Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan; used for electricity generation.
 
• **Peat:** Least carbon content; found in small quantities.
 
 
 
• **Coal Mining in India:**
 
 
• Managed primarily by **Coal India Limited (CIL)**, a government-owned entity.
 
• India’s coal production reached **893.08 million tonnes** in **2022-23**.
 
• Coal blocks are allocated to private players under **auction schemes**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Coal mining leads to deforestation, soil erosion, and air pollution.
 
• Efforts are being made to promote **clean coal technologies** and renewable energy sources to reduce dependency on coal.
